## Learning goals

This week, you will get an overview of the course, and introductions to omics data and the Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC). More specifically, you will learn:

#### [**Course intro**](./w1_1_course-intro.qmd) (Tuesday class)

- What to expect from this course
- Which tools and languages we will use
- What is expected of you during this course
- Get up to speed on the infrastructure of the course

#### [**Omics data**](./w1_2_omics-data.qmd) (Tuesday/Thursday class)

- What omics data is
- About the main high-throughput sequencing technologies
- How Illumina sequence libraries are structured
- What reference genomes are, and what they are good for
- What the main sequence file types are and what FASTA and FASTQ files look like

#### [**The Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC)**](./w1_3_osc.qmd) (Thursday class)

- What a supercomputer is and why they are useful
- What resources the Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC) provides
- How to access OSC resources through its OnDemand webportal

## Readings

### Required readings

- @poinsignon2023: *Working with omics data: An interdisciplinary challenge at the crossroads of biology and computer science*
- @markowetz2015: *Five selfish reasons to work reproducibly*

### Optional readings

Throughout the course, chapters from these two books are optional readings for this course. Both can be accessed online for free with OSU credentials via the links below.

- @buffalo2015: [Bioinformatics Data Skills (Buffalo 2015)](https://search.library.osu.edu/permalink/01OHIOLINK_OSU/1oqfg3i/alma991085518416808507) ("**Buffalo**" for short) \
    This week: Preface and Chapter 1 -- *How to Learn Bioinformatics*

- @allesina2019: [Computing Skills for Biologists (Allesina & Wilmes 2019)](https://search.library.osu.edu/permalink/01OHIOLINK_OSU/1oqfg3i/alma991085456156508507) ("**CSB**" for short)\
    This week: Chapter 0 -- *Building a Computing Toolbox* (Introduction & Section 0.1 only)

### Further resources

Browse through these titles and see if any of these spark your interest --- many of these present omics and HTS data in a more field-specific light, e.g. plant pathology. **Bolded** entries are especially highly recommended.

- @lee2023: ***The principles and applications of high-throughput sequencing technologies***
  ([link](https://www.ksdb.org/archive/view_article?pid=dr-27-1-9))
- @dijk2023: ***Genomics in the long-read sequencing era*** ([link](https://www-cell-com.proxy.lib.ohio-state.edu/trends/genetics/fulltext/S0168-9525(23)00119-1))
- @vonderheyden2025: *Advancing species conservation and management through omics tools* ([link](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/1755-0998.14123))
- @nizamani2023: *High-throughput sequencing in plant disease management: a comprehensive review of benefits, challenges, and future perspectives* ([link](https://phytopatholres.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s42483-023-00199-5))
- @aragona2022: *New-generation sequencing technology in diagnosis of fungal plant pathogens: A dream comes true?* ([link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9320658/))
- @mahmood2022: *Multi-omics revolution to promote plant breeding efficiency* ([link](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1062952/full))
- @rai2019: *A new era in plant functional genomics* ([link](https://www-sciencedirect-com.proxy.lib.ohio-state.edu/science/article/pii/S2452310019300216))
- @pinto2024: *Sequencing-based analysis of microbiomes* ([link](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-024-00746-6))
- @manzoni2018: *Genome, transcriptome and proteome: the rise of omics data and their integration in biomedical sciences* ([link](https://academic.oup.com/bib/article/19/2/286/2562648))
